south-downs-way-50.course: From Hillbarn Recreation Ground in Worthing, joining the South Downs Way before Chanctonbury Ring and finishing in Eastbourne.
south-downs-way-50.start: Registration at Worthing College; start at adjacent Hillbarn Recreation Ground, BN14 9QF.
south-downs-way-50.rules: A previous organised marathon-distance finish within its limit is required. Intermediate aid-station cut-offs apply.
south-downs-way-50.transport: Free start parking. The finish-to-start shuttle must be booked separately.
south-downs-way-50.facilities: Start toilets, water and changing; finish showers and hot food; seven aid stations including the finish.

loch-ness-marathon.course: Point-to-point from moorland between Fort Augustus and Whitebridge, along Loch Ness through Foyers, then into Inverness; a climb around mile 17 interrupts the net downhill profile.
loch-ness-marathon.start: 10:00 remote start. Organiser coaches depart Inverness Ice Centre from 07:30 to 07:50; arrive between 07:00 and 07:30.
loch-ness-marathon.rules: Collect the race pack on Saturday 25 September at Bught Park with photo ID. There is no private or spectator vehicle access to the start.
loch-ness-marathon.transport: Organiser coach from Inverness Ice Centre is included and does not need pre-booking. Other lochside pickups require advance booking; finish is in Inverness.
loch-ness-marathon.facilities: Start-to-finish baggage transfer; seven water and four gel stations on the course.

inverness-half-marathon.course: Road half marathon starting on Bught Road and finishing by the Bught Park event village; water at miles 3, 6, 9 and 11.5.
inverness-half-marathon.start: Bught Road, IV3 5SS at 10:30; event village information desk opens at 08:30.
inverness-half-marathon.rules: Minimum age 17. Road sections begin reopening after 12:30; runners may be guided onto the pavement.
inverness-half-marathon.transport: Limited parking at Inverness Leisure and council car parks; do not park at Inverness Ice Centre or on the route.
inverness-half-marathon.facilities: Four on-course water stations plus finish water; posted UK race packs and an event village information desk.

london-marathon.cutoff: Saturday finish closes 17:30; Sunday secondary finish closes 23:59:59
london-marathon.course: From Greenwich and Blackheath via Cutty Sark, central London and the Thames to The Mall; the same route is planned on both 2027 days.
london-marathon.start: Greenwich/Blackheath. Saturday is expected to start about 09:00 and Sunday about 09:30; individual wave times will be issued later.
london-marathon.rules: 2027 Saturday and Sunday allocations cannot be exchanged. Saturday finish closes at 17:30; the Sunday secondary finish closes at 23:59:59.
london-marathon.transport: Multiple start areas at Greenwich/Blackheath and a central London finish; use your assigned start and wave travel instructions.
london-marathon.facilities: Course toilets, drinks and pacers are described by the organiser; the final 2027 station layout is still to be issued.

west-highland-way-race.cutoff: 35 hours, with strict intermediate checkpoint cut-offs
west-highland-way-race.course: Approximately 95 miles point-to-point along the West Highland Way from Milngavie to Fort William via Balmaha, Tyndrum, Glencoe and Kinlochleven.
west-highland-way-race.start: 01:00 from Milngavie railway station car park after late-evening registration and briefing.
west-highland-way-race.rules: 2027 qualification requires at least 90 miles across no more than two eligible off-road ultras. Final 2027 rules are due in May.
west-highland-way-race.transport: Point-to-point Milngavie to Fort William; support crew and return travel need advance planning.

devil-o-the-highlands-footrace.course: 42-mile point-to-point West Highland Way trail from Tyndrum to Fort William via Glencoe and Kinlochleven; approximately 1,981m of ascent.
devil-o-the-highlands-footrace.start: 06:00 from Tyndrum on 24 April 2027; early and previous-evening registration are listed.
devil-o-the-highlands-footrace.rules: Carry a waterproof jacket, emergency foil blanket and charged phone. Four checkpoints and a 12-hour limit; check final cut-off rules.
devil-o-the-highlands-footrace.transport: Bookable Fort William-to-Tyndrum and return buses have limited capacity. Long-stay Tyndrum parking is restricted.
devil-o-the-highlands-footrace.facilities: Four checkpoints, two checkpoint food drop bags, finish-bag transfer and finish showers.

cardiff-half-marathon.course: Closed-road Cardiff city-centre half marathon with a Castle Street start; consult the organiser map for the current route and water stations.
cardiff-half-marathon.start: Castle Street from 10:00, with colour-coded starting pens and staggered waves.
cardiff-half-marathon.rules: The 2027 general-entry ballot has closed; charity and other organiser-listed routes may remain. Do not swap race numbers.
cardiff-half-marathon.transport: Central Cardiff road closures affect arrival; check the organiser travel and parking plan.
cardiff-half-marathon.facilities: Bag drop on Museum Avenue from 08:30 for one labelled small backpack; toilets at the event village, start and water stations.

omagh-half-marathon.course: Half marathon and 5K routes from Omagh Leisure Complex; verify the distance-specific map before travel.
omagh-half-marathon.start: Omagh Leisure Complex; distance-specific assembly and start times to confirm.
omagh-half-marathon.rules: Check 2027 runner instructions for age limits, timing and collection arrangements.
omagh-half-marathon.transport: Start and finish at Omagh Leisure Complex; check local access and parking notices.

maverick-peak-district-x-trail.course: Five marked Peak District routes from Bakewell Showground over moorland, gritstone edges, woodland trails and river valleys.
maverick-peak-district-x-trail.start: Bakewell Showground, DE45 1AH; 55km and marathon at 08:00, 28km at 09:00, shorter routes at 10:00.
maverick-peak-district-x-trail.rules: The 55km has a strict 10-hour limit and intermediate outpost deadlines. Race packs are collected on event morning; no dogs are allowed.
maverick-peak-district-x-trail.facilities: Longer routes have outposts for food and water; the 10km and 6km have no outpost. Bring a refillable cup or bottle.

race-to-the-stones.course: The Ridgeway routes offer 50km and 100km choices, with approximately 1,350m of gain on the full 100km. The 50km variants cover different halves of the course.
race-to-the-stones.start: Distance-specific start points and times differ; use the 2027 route page and eventual participant guide before travel.
race-to-the-stones.rules: Choose the 50km variant and non-stop or two-day 100km format before comparing cut-offs and travel. The organiser marks the route.
race-to-the-stones.transport: Point-to-point options require a finish plan; organiser shuttles can be booked separately.

alloa-half-marathon.course: 13.1-mile road race through Alloa and the Hillfoots; 2027 traffic arrangements remain subject to final approval.
alloa-half-marathon.start: Alloa start and finish; final registration and start timings are due in the race instructions.
alloa-half-marathon.rules: Follow the final 2027 race instructions for timing, access and road closures.

richmond-park-half-marathon.course: Four laps on marked trail paths, pavement and grass within Richmond Park; rolling hills mean the repeated climbs matter.
richmond-park-half-marathon.start: Sheen Gate, Richmond TW10 5HT; half marathon at 09:30 and 10K at 10:10.
richmond-park-half-marathon.rules: Minimum age 17 for the half. No formal cut-off, but the organiser asks runners expecting over three hours to arrange course support.
richmond-park-half-marathon.facilities: Bag drop, chip timing, finish refreshments and race photos are listed by the organiser.

snowdonia-trail-ultra-eryri.cutoff: 11 hours 30 minutes, with staged course cut-offs
snowdonia-trail-ultra-eryri.course: Mountain route from Llanberis up toward Yr Wyddfa, through remote trails and the Dinorwig slate landscape, finishing in Llanberis.
snowdonia-trail-ultra-eryri.start: Usually 05:00 from Llanberis; the confirmed time and registration arrangements will appear in final instructions.
snowdonia-trail-ultra-eryri.rules: Minimum age 20, mandatory mountain kit and staged cut-offs; late arrivals at two course splits are diverted to the marathon route.

beacons-way-ultra-100.course: Approximately 100 miles across Bannau Brycheiniog from Abergavenny Castle to Llangadog, via the Black Mountains, Pen-y-Fan and Carmarthen Fans.
beacons-way-ultra-100.start: 06:00 from Abergavenny Castle, NP7 5EE; registration and mandatory tracker collection precede the start.
beacons-way-ultra-100.rules: Minimum age 20; prior organised 50-mile ultra and mountain experience required. Self-navigation with map and compass is expected.
beacons-way-ultra-100.transport: Point-to-point finish at Llangadog RFC. Optional organiser return transport is available; plan crew and finish collection.
beacons-way-ultra-100.facilities: Ten checkpoints with food and drink, medical support and live GPS tracking.

newport-marathon.course: Fully closed-road marathon starting and finishing on Newport's riverfront; check the current route map for detailed turns.
newport-marathon.start: Usk Way near the University of South Wales; marathon start listed at 09:00, event information opens at 07:00.
newport-marathon.rules: General marathon entries are sold out; organiser-listed charity and bundle places may remain. Follow the 2027 participant guide for pen and timing rules.
newport-marathon.transport: Central riverfront start and finish; plan for city-centre road closures and use the organiser travel guidance.

norn-iron-100-half-marathon.course: Point-to-point North Coast Ulster Way from Ballintoy to Portballintrae, passing the Giant's Causeway area.
norn-iron-100-half-marathon.start: 08:00 at Ballintoy; organiser bus from Portballintrae has a time still to be confirmed.
norn-iron-100-half-marathon.rules: Follow existing Ulster Way markers; no extra signs or course marshals except at the water refill point. Download the organiser GPX.
norn-iron-100-half-marathon.transport: Finish and bus pickup at Portballintrae; confirm the bus departure before arranging travel to Ballintoy.
norn-iron-100-half-marathon.facilities: Medical cover and post-race snack; a mid-route water refill point supplies no bottles or cups.

porthcawl-10k.course: Closed-road seaside 10K via Rest Bay, Trecco Bay, Coney Bay and the town centre, starting from Porthcawl Esplanade.
porthcawl-10k.start: 10:00 on Porthcawl Esplanade; junior races follow from 12:15.
porthcawl-10k.rules: Race number with embedded timing chip is posted before the event. Buggies are restricted to the Fun Run.
porthcawl-10k.transport: Pre-bookable town parking has limited capacity; allow for road closures and follow event signage from M4 junction 37.
porthcawl-10k.facilities: Bag storage on The Portway, on-course water, pacers and an event village.

skyline-scotland-utmb.course: Mountain trail race formats around the Nevis Range; 2027 distances and final GPX routes are still to be confirmed.
skyline-scotland-utmb.start: Event programme is scheduled for September 2027; exact race starts and registration depend on format.
skyline-scotland-utmb.rules: The organiser says details of 2027 formats and registration are pending. Do not rely on previous-edition routes or kit lists.
